title: AI Resume Screening Automation: How to Build It in 2026
summary: AI resume screening automation requires connecting your candidate storage to a reasoning engine and your tracking system for faster shortlisting.
body_markdown:
## Building the automated screening workflow in Activepieces


Activepieces places an Agent step alongside deterministic automation steps inside one flow definition, using a visual canvas to link document storage, AI reasoning, and spreadsheet logging into a single autonomous sequence.


While executive teams often expect recruiters to manually prompt LLMs for every applicant, this workflow automates the heavy lifting by triggering a rubric-based evaluation the moment a file hits a shared folder.


Judgment and rules run in the same flow, on the same engine, in the same run trace.


Open the flow builder, place an Agent step alongside a deterministic automation step in the same flow, then open the run trace, one execution logged, start to finish, not two systems bridged by a callback.


> Judgment and rules run in the same flow, on the same engine, in the same run trace.


### Setting up the Google Drive folder trigger


Assigning a unique Folder ID ensures the automation only reacts to new resumes rather than every document in the cloud. The pipeline begins with the Google Drive "New File in Folder" trigger, which monitors a specific directory dedicated to incoming applications.


This prevents the system from burning API credits on unrelated administrative files. When a user uploads a PDF, Activepieces captures the file metadata and content to pass it to the next stage of the sequence.


### Sending resume PDFs to OpenAI for scoring


The "Ask Assistant" action in the OpenAI integration receives the resume text and compares it against a standardized rubric using GPT-6 Astra.


This model has complex reasoning capabilities. These allow it to move beyond keyword matching to evaluate whether a candidate’s experience actually aligns with the senior-level requirements defined in the prompt.


### Step 3: Log the candidate's name, score, and justification in Google Sheets


To record the candidate’s name, their numerical score, and the AI’s qualitative justification, the final action uses the Google Sheets "Insert Row" integration.


This centralizes the data so that a recruiter can sort by the highest scores at the start of their day, effectively ignoring the bottom 80% of the pile.


This step transforms the raw output of an LLM into a structured database, allowing the team to track hiring velocity and rubric accuracy over time.


### Step 4: Testing the first live resume execution


Before activating the flow, the "Test flow" button allows the recruiter to run a sample resume through the canvas to verify that the logic holds.


The Activepieces builder displays the execution path in real-time, showing a green checkmark for successful steps or a red error message if a connection fails.


Every agent tool call, the data it acted on, and the order it made its decisions in is traced step by step, alongside the deterministic flow steps running next to it.


Check the Run Details and Debugging UI for the per-step agent decision trace, and the audit logs and event-streaming feature for how it exports to a SIEM.


You will see the exact input and output JSON for each step in the left panel. A recruiter can see exactly why a specific run might have failed (for example, an expired Gmail connection or an incorrectly mapped "Receiver Email" field).


The screenshot of the builder canvas demonstrates this visibility. The left panel shows the exact input and output JSON for each step.

If a run fails, the "Edit Run" button at the bottom is for immediate troubleshooting without losing the data from that specific applicant.


Once the test run confirms that the sheet logs the candidate's score and justification correctly, the flow is ready for production.
